question: Was Ibn Turka an original philosopher on the model of a European rationalist?
proposition: Ibn Turka deserves to be called the 'Spinoza of Iran': a major independent thinker whose works ought to be edited and studied.
scholar: Muḥammad Taqī Dānishpazhūh (as reported by Melvin-Koushki)
reasoning: The characterization is, per MK, rhetorical: it underscores the need to publish and study his works (pdf p.24 n.17; p.38), a call Bihbahani repeated.
MK's objection is irony, not denial of the call: Spinoza, as Bible critic, undercut the basis on which lettrism rests, so the title is unfitting (p.24 n.17).

Dānishpazhūh 'too recognized in passing' the importance of lettrism to Ibn Turka (p.38), so he is not a pure representative of the Tamhid-centred reading. MK is a partisan reporter. Confidence records how fully the pages of MK's dissertation let us reconstruct this position and its grounds, not whether it is true.
